actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The card's primary model is assets/xmls/particle/main.xml: its root is a <mujoco> element whose worldbody contains the body 'particle' with three slide joints named slide0, slide1 and slide2 on the x, y and z axes
The model's <option> element sets the integration timestep to 0.005 s
slide0 and slide1 have damping 0.1, while slide2 has damping 10000
The particle body has a sphere geom of mass 1, half-size 0.15 and position 0 0 0
The model declares two <motor> actuators with gear 100 on slide0 and slide1, and neither actuator states a ctrlrange, so the model file gives the two controls no limit
The README says actions in the action_space are all actuators of objects added during world building, and names ObjFromXML('particle') as an object with actuators
The README states that worldgen uses meters, kilograms and radians, with angles in [-pi, pi]
The README says the repository requires the MuJoCo physics engine, was tested with MuJoCo 1.50 and installs through mujoco-py
The repository is archived and its code is provided as-is with no updates expected
The simple_particle example loads the 'particle' object with ObjFromXML and builds a 4 x 4 x 2.5 world
The simple_particle example runs the environment with horizon 30
ctrl_set_action copies a torque actuator's action into sim.data.ctrl, and adds the current qpos for a position actuator
When no explicit action bounds are given, Env's action space has nmocap * 7 + model.nu entries
Env.step clamps the action to the action space, calls set_action and then sim.step

determinism.notes: the model starts from the MJCF defaults and MuJoCo integrates deterministically; the bridge accepts cap.world.reset.v1 seed for the class contract but mj_resetData does not use it, so no seed selects a different state

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model file for the two actuators, the three slide joints and the 0.005 s timestep, but integrates a placeholder joint motion proportional to each control value, so trajectories, damping, gear forces and actuator dynamics are not MuJoCo's
the stand-in resolves no contact, constraint or friction (the model's only geom contact is the mass-1 sphere against the mass-0 outer-bound box) and loads no rendering context
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

the upstream world-generation layer (WorldBuilder, placements, randomization) and the Env wrapper are not part of this driver: it serves the bare MJCF model and its ctrl vector, not a generated world or a Gym environment
the card's second model (assets/xmls/particle_hinge/main.xml) is not served: one package serves one device, and this driver uses the card's models[0]
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
